name: Data_FindNextRowMatchingConditions
summary: Advances the cursor to the next row of the 0x14-byte condition table: skips rows whose type byte does not match *cursor, requires the row flag bit in the save work and the per-row flag byte, then walks the row's compact condition list (opcodes 0x19..0x22) against the selected party member's fields (+0x664, +0x668, +0x66C, +0x3EC and +0x370+0x2F5..0x2FB). On a match it stores the row index in cursor+4; otherwise it writes the FF FF FF 7F end marker.
evidence: The whole body is the evaluator: data-manager/work getters, the 0x14-byte stride, the 0x19..0x22 switch against the member record and the explicit cursor[4..7] end marker. No caller-specific data is used, so the neutral Data_ prefix and the row-scan verb describe exactly what it does for every caller.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_UpdateEffectsB
summary: Damaged second copy of the member-widget effect update: compares the widget effect-index getter (vtable +0x60) with the actor getter (+0x48) across the actor count from 0x00630D64 and either recreates the effect handle through Svc_ResolveObjectHandle or calls Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_CalcAnchor. The decompiler lost r6/r7/r10 and truncates with halt_baddata, so only the function family is certain.
evidence: The body is built from unaff_r6/r7/r10 and ends in halt_baddata(); the callee set matches 0x003CBB1C. Under the Ghidra-trap rule a damaged body keeps maybe_ and confidence at or below 0.3.

name: Field_Object2D_RestartStateEffect
summary: Stops the object's current state effect (Effect_ReleaseHandle on self->f_2E8), rebuilds the effect transform from the object position at f_9C..f_A4 (mirroring the global at 0x007E7024 when f_2D8 is clear) and recreates effect id 0x4B5 via Effect_FindOrCreateInstance, storing the new handle back in f_2E8. Called by Field_Object2D_UpdateEffectSlot when the object's state effect has to be restarted.
evidence: The body explicitly releases f_2E8, builds the transform and recreates effect 0x4B5 into f_2E8; its caller is the named Field_Object2D_UpdateEffectSlot. The only inference left is the 'restart' framing, which the release-then-recreate order supports.

name: maybe_Gfx_EffectNodeCreateChild_75B0D4
summary: Child-object factory of one effect/scene node class (parent vtable 0x00773540, child vtable 0x75B0D4): opens with the same call as the other copies (0x005F541C), allocates a 0xAC-byte child from the parent allocator (f_48), initialises the member pair with the child vtable and the parent back-pointer, and constructs two 0x40-byte sub-objects. On OOM it reports through the global error block at 0x00725E4C and returns with f_4C = 0.
evidence: The 0xAC allocation, base-constructor call, vtable store, parent back-pointer and std_ConstructArray of two 0x40-byte objects are identical to 0x004B143C and 0x004B1F74, so the 'one child factory per node subclass' pattern is established; nothing identifies the concrete child class behind vtable 0x75B0D4, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Text_Row_GetScaleFactorA
summary: Returns a per-row-type float multiplier for a battle text/bar row: probes the row type through virtual +0xE8 for the id group 0x1E, 0x1F, 0xA2, 0xAB, 0xAE, 0x20, 0x21, 0x101, 0x114 and 0x11C, reads a value for that type through 0x00491270 (default 100.0), scales it by 0.01f and marks the layout dirty when the result is non-zero. Callers multiply a row value by the returned s0 float.
evidence: Assembly at the call sites is `mov r0,#<rowType>; bl 0x491270; vmov.f32 s16,s0`, i.e. exactly one row-type argument and a float result, and Ghidra shows void only because it dropped the s0 return (FACTS VFP trap). The two verified callers (0x004937C4 and 0x004948B0, bl sites checked in asm) multiply by in_s0, so the getter role is solid. NOTE for follow-up: the merged name of 0x00491270, Battle_CalcRandomDamageVariance, does not fit a one-argument row-type call; it behaves like a shared table-row float helper and should be re-examined.

name: maybe_Text_Row_GetScaleFactorC
summary: Second per-row-type float multiplier for a battle text/bar row: probes the row type through virtual +0xE8 for the id group beginning 0x23, 0x24, 0xA3, 0xAC, 0xAF, 0x25, 0x26 (then 0x115, 0x107, 0x102 and a computed +8 id), reads a value for that type through 0x00491270 (default 100.0), scales it by 0.01f and marks the layout dirty when the result is non-zero. Callers multiply a row value by the returned s0 float.
evidence: Same shape as 0x00497FD4: one row-type argument to 0x00491270, float result in s0 (Ghidra drops it), and the callers 0x00494AC0 and 0x00495B2C have bl sites inside their bodies (0x00494AF0/0x494B58 and 0x00495C34/0x495C50, checked in asm) and consume the float as a multiplier. The two functions differ only in the row-type id group, hence the A/C suffix retained for disambiguation.

name: Battle_Row_UpdateFromActorSlot
signature: void Battle_Row_UpdateFromActorSlot(int rowTableId, void* ctx, int clipBand)
summary: Updates one battle message row from the four ctx actor slots: initialises the row layout from rowTableId, finds the slot whose actor f_768 equals the row-template entry, scales the row's current value (ctx->f_18) by the template factor and pushes it through the text row helpers (Text_BuildRowForTarget, Text_UpdateRowBlink, Text_MarkLayoutDirty). Caller Text_MeasureRowByType uses it while re-measuring rows.
evidence: Caller Text_MeasureRowByType and callees Text_BuildRowForTarget/Text_UpdateRowBlink/Text_MarkLayoutDirty are named, and the body's four-slot loop plus the f_768 match implement exactly 'take this row's value from the matching actor slot'. There is no maximum/aggregation (the old MaxActorValue wording was wrong), so the current name fits the body.

name: maybe_Gfx_EffectNodeCreateChild_75B164
summary: Child-object factory of a second effect/scene node class (parent vtable 0x007767C0, child vtable 0x75B164): opens with the same call as its sibling copies (0x005F2B54), allocates a 0xAC-byte child, initialises the member pair with the child vtable and parent back-pointer and constructs two 0x40-byte sub-objects; the OOM report reads the global animation-name block. Child class still unknown.
evidence: Third copy of the same template (with 0x004721C4 and 0x004B1F74): identical allocation/ctor/vtable/back-pointer/sub-object sequence. That proves the factory pattern only; the concrete child class is not named anywhere in the body, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Fs_Archive_OpenRecordByPath
signature: u32 maybe_Fs_Archive_OpenRecordByPath(void* self, u32* out, int* typeAndIndex)
summary: Opens one archive entry by name: resolves the UTF-16 path with Fs_Archive_ResolvePath, folds the name into a 64-bit rotate-xor hash seeded with 0x075BCD15, looks it up with Fs_Archive_FindFile (retrying as a directory for the 0x11/0x6F 'not a file' result), then allocates a 0x30-byte accessor node from the pool at 0x007E7B58, fills its offset/size and owner and calls its virtual +0x18. Returns 0 or the Fs error code.
evidence: The body is entirely archive path/hash/lookup work (Fs_Archive_ResolvePath, Fs_Archive_FindFile, Fs_Archive_FindDirectory) plus the pool node with vtable 0x00780E18; there is no service-content API in it, so the Svc_Content_ prefix was unsupported and the new name states what is actually opened.

name: Snd_StreamManager_Update
summary: Per-frame update of the streamed-audio manager: advances the five fade records (f_1AB0 bitmask, f_1AB4 array), updates all stream slots and voices through Snd_StreamSlot_UpdateAll and Snd_StreamVoice_Update, flushes the texture uploads it owns and releases finished ones, then retires an expired handle at f_60.
evidence: The two dominant callees are the named stream helpers Snd_StreamSlot_UpdateAll (0x00105584) and Snd_StreamVoice_Update (0x00105AFC), and the body's fade bitmask/array and stream/voice-slot state are consistent with a stream manager frame update. The trailing Gfx upload calls are shared frame bookkeeping, not the function's purpose.

name: Gfx_ReleaseRenderContext
summary: Releases the frame's display channel (Pack_HandleTable_Get on the caller handle followed by Gfx_ReleaseDisplayChannel) and destroys the renderer object stored at self->f_18 through its vtable slot +4, clearing the pointer. Part of the engine teardown path.
evidence: The body is the two-step release (display channel, then vtable+4 destruction of f_18) and the only direct call site is 0x001026A8 inside Engine_Initialize, i.e. the engine shutdown path. The renderer at f_18 is only ever destroyed here, so the name describes the visible effect.

name: maybe_Engine_SubmitFrameEntries
summary: Frame step: pumps the sound voice list (maybe_Snd_UpdateVoiceList), then, when the global 0x007AE18C is set, calls vtable +0x20 on every object in the self->f_54..f_58 array (8-byte stride) with the fixed frame arguments (0x3F, stack buffer, 0x100, 10). Called once from Engine_Initialize; the queued object class is not identified.
evidence: The body is only the sound voice-list pump plus an indirect 8-byte-strided vtable+0x20 loop; there is no draw-list construction, so the old Gfx_SubmitDrawList wording was unsupported, and 'submit frame entries' remains a description of the loop rather than a proven role.

name: maybe_Fs_Channel_InitFields
signature: u32 maybe_Fs_Channel_InitFields(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Initialises one transfer channel of the large cache/heap object: stores the channel pointer at +0xE114, initialises the wait event at +0xE118 (Os_LightEvent_Init) and submits a 0x2000-byte staging buffer with mode 0x11 and handle -2 through Gfx_CommandBuffer_Submit; returns 1. Called from Engine_Initialize and InitHeaps.
evidence: The body is a three-field initialiser over the +0xE1xx block (pointer, event, command buffer) and returns 1; the 'Fs_Channel' owner and the meaning of the +0xE1xx fields are still inferred from the two init callers, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_WaitSyncSubmitNoLock
signature: int maybe_Gfx_WaitSyncSubmitNoLock(u32 request, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Lock-free inner half of Gfx_WaitSyncSubmit: first waits for the display/IPC state to leave the transient values (it sets state 9 and spins), then sends the request through Svc_SendRequest2, retrying on the 0xC8A0CC02 / 0xE0A0CC08 / 0xC8A0CFF0 busy results with a 10,000,000-tick sleep between attempts; returns the final result.
evidence: The sibling 0x00107D00 is named Gfx_WaitSyncSubmit and uses the same three busy result codes; this 352-byte function is the retry loop that does the waiting and submitting, while 0x00107D00 is the small wrapper. Nothing calls it directly (likely inlined), and the 'Gfx' attribution comes from the sibling, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Os_WaitIpcTransferDone
summary: Waits for an asynchronous IPC transfer to finish: under the global monitor 0x007E7A70 it polls the completion object at 0x007AEA24, sleeps while the status is the 0xD0401834/busy value, then retires the record with 0x0011CC7C and re-sends it through Svc_SendRequestBuffer128; re-arms the wait object when the record is not in state 2 or 5.
evidence: The body uses only OS primitives (Os_LockMonitor, Os_LightEvent_Init, Os_LockSemaphore, Svc_SendRequestBuffer128) and is tail-entered from 0x00118918/0x0011895C in the 0x00118814 path; there is no sound-specific call, so the 'Snd_' attribution had no support. The record states 2/5 and the busy code are generic IPC states.

name: maybe_Engine_InitIpcWorker
summary: Brings up an IPC worker block: clears the state words, creates or reuses the handle at f_2C, initialises its event, queries the IPC state flags, sends the unit/status request, installs the 0x1000-byte transfer buffer (0x0011E6F8) and the completion callback, then creates the worker thread 0x0011F3C0 with this block as argument and releases the monitor.
evidence: The body is a complete worker bring-up and its tail calls Os_CreateThreadWithStack(&self->f_6C,...,0x0011F3C0,&self), which fixes the init/loop pair. The inherited 'Snd_' prefix had no support in the body, and the Gfx attribution also came from neighbours the asm does not confirm (Gfx_WriteHwRegsMasked is only called from 0x00113894), so the subsystem stays unnamed.

name: Mem_PoolAllocNode
summary: Pops one node off the object pool's free list (pool+0x24), increments the live count (pool+0x2C) under the pool monitor (pool+0x30) and, when the pool flag bit 0 is set, relocates the node into the pool window via 0x00118B28; returns NULL when the pool is exhausted.
evidence: All the named callers are the Svc object constructors (0x00505058, 0x005055C8, 0x005056E0, 0x00505804 and Gfx_GetCommandSlot), and the body is the exact inverse of the named release path (push onto +0x24, decrement +0x2C, same +0x30 monitor). The node payload type is unknown, but the pool-allocator role is established.

name: Text_NgWord_ValidationWorker
summary: Thread body of the text NG-word filter: while the enable byte (worker+4) is set it takes the monitor at worker+0x444, consumes one queued request (flag bit 0 = validate all, bit 1 = validate one), runs Text_NgWord_ValidateAll or Text_NgWord_ValidateOne with the filter state at worker+0x10, stores the result/error bytes at worker+0xC/0xD, drops the request and sleeps 1,000,000 ticks when idle.
evidence: The two callees are named and their own headers state they are part of this worker: Text_NgWord_ValidateAll (0.60) loads ngword:/%d.txt dictionaries and Text_NgWord_ValidateOne (0.55) masks one UTF-16 field; both are called only from 0x001DBD58. The old 'Fs_AsyncLoadWorker' name described seek/read work that is absent from the body.

name: Os_UnlockMonitor
summary: Recursive monitor release used at the end of locked sections: takes the monitor lock, and when the state byte f_76 is not 2 it marks the monitor contended, releases the raw lock (0x00117ED0) and waits on the semaphore at +100; otherwise it clears f_76, decrements the recursion count at +8 and, when that reaches zero, clears the owner at +4 and wakes all waiters (Os_EventSetAll).
evidence: 91 call sites (70 named) are always paired with Os_LockMonitor, and the body is the recursive unlock protocol (f_76 state, +8 recursion, +4 owner, EventSetAll). The earlier objection is consistent with the name: 0x00117ED0 is the raw release used inside this wrapper, while this function also handles the contended/waiter hand-off.

name: maybe_Snd_InitStreamContext
summary: Creates or attaches the streaming context: opens the kernel handle at *ctx if absent, tags it through maybe_Snd_SetUnitFlagBit, queries the unit count (0x00112384) into ctx[1], sets the 0x2000 transfer buffer, resets the 24 channel objects and restores channel/unit defaults on the re-init path. Returns 0 or a Horizon error code.
evidence: The init half is readable through the named maybe_Snd_* channel helpers and the 24-channel/0x2000-buffer layout, but the context type is not named by any caller (no named caller in the readable tree), so 'stream context' and the 'Snd_' prefix remain hypotheses.

name: maybe_Engine_IpcWorker
summary: Worker thread body of the 0x34-byte IPC request ring initialised by 0x00119498: waits on the worker event, pops one record (with an exclusive-access index update), dispatches it through the callback table at worker+0x10 and, for record type 1, signals the waiting thread; exits when the stop byte at worker+0x77 is set.
evidence: 0x00119498 passes this exact address as the Os_CreateThreadWithStack entry (visible in that function's tail), so the two are the init/loop pair. The body itself only uses OS primitives and the callback table and has no sound-specific call, so neither 'Snd_' nor a graphics subsystem can be claimed.

name: maybe_Snd_TeardownStreamContext
summary: Tears a streaming context down: sends stop request 2 with mode 1 or 3, waits for the transfer-done flag, clears the active byte f_4C7, releases the 0x1080-byte sample buffer when asked, closes the handle (svcCloseHandle) and returns the cached error at ctx[1].
evidence: The request/wait/close sequence mirrors the init path and the 0x1080-byte buffer release matches the sample buffer; no named caller pins the owning service, so the 'Snd_' prefix stays a hypothesis.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelFilterParams
signature: void maybe_Snd_SetChannelFilterParams(u32 unit, u16* unitA, u16* unitB, u32 flags, ...)
summary: Writes the caller's u16 filter/pan words into the sound-unit record (unitA[0x17], [0x22]..[0x2B] and beyond) and pushes them to the command stream through the sound filter setters; the 18-byte Thumb decompilation is damaged (in_CY, overlapping varargs), so the argument list and record layout are unreliable.
evidence: This is an 18-byte Thumb function whose decompilation is damaged and whose parameters overlap; the only basis for the name is the sound filter setter tail. Per the damaged-body rule it keeps maybe_ and confidence at or below 0.3.

name: maybe_Svc_Cfg_ReleaseServiceU
summary: Releases one reference to the cfg/session service: decrements the user count at 0x007AF0EC+8 under the config monitor and, when it reaches zero, closes the handle in 0x007AF0F8 with svcCloseHandle and resets it to the sentinel. Identical to the kind==0 arm of 0x0011212C.
evidence: The globals, refcount and close sequence are identical to the kind==0 arm of 0x0011212C, so the 'release one reference' description is right; which service the handle belongs to cannot be read from the body (the named callers span sound, movie and gfx code), so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Os_ReleaseSharedHandle
summary: Releases one reference to the shared kernel handle at 0x007AF900: when the refcount at 0x007AF8F8+4 drops below 2 it closes the handle with svcCloseHandle, decrements the count and restores the process-handle sentinel 0x00741AD4; otherwise it only decrements and returns the 0x082067F0 status constant.
evidence: The body is the same refcount-and-close shape as the cfg helpers in this batch (count, handle in a global slot, svcCloseHandle, sentinel restore); the only caller (0x0011E0DC) is unnamed, so the handle owner stays unknown.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieQueue_Peek
summary: Copies the next queued movie-frame descriptor out of the ring under the global movie monitor 0x007CF360: surface id, two converted addresses, three timestamp words and the per-frame words indexed by the read index, and returns 1; returns 0 when the queue is empty. The read index (f_34) is not advanced, so it is a peek.
evidence: The body writes exactly the frame descriptor fields from f_28/f_2c indexed by f_34 and never updates f_34, confirming a read-only peek; the frame-ring shape matches the movie track code, but no named caller confirms the queue class.

name: maybe_Gfx_ExchangeSlotValue
summary: Atomically exchanges one of seven 32-bit slots at +0x10 of the draw-state object (singleton 0x007AF178->f_1C) under that object's monitor and returns the previous content; slot >= 7 is ignored and returns 0.
evidence: The seven-slot array, the monitor and the returned old value are all explicit in the body; the meaning of the slots (surfaces, command slots, ...) is still unknown, so the name stays at mechanism level and keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Fs_SeekStream
signature: u32 maybe_Fs_SeekStream(void* stream, u32 posLo, u32 posHi, u32 limit)
summary: Seeks the stream: if the target 64-bit position (posLo:posHi) lies within [0, end] it stores the new current/end/hint pairs, calls the owner's vtable +0x40 seek callback and clears the pending event; returns 1 when the seek was accepted, 0 otherwise.
evidence: The 64-bit bound check, the four stored position/hint pairs and the owner callback at vtable +0x40 are readable; nothing names the owner as a file stream and there is no named caller, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Svc_SetFieldLocked
summary: Stores value into object+0x180 while holding the monitor at object+0x184; a plain published-field setter under a lock.
evidence: The three-instruction body is unambiguous as a locked setter, but the field meaning is unknown and there is no named caller, so the 'Svc_' attribution and the field name remain guesses.

name: maybe_Mem_HeapFreeLocked
summary: Frees a block through the heap stored in the handle: takes the monitor at heap+0x58 around the free call 0x0050E5B8 and returns. The free helper is itself still named maybe_Text_Font_ReleaseRef (0.45), which is suspect.
evidence: The body is handle+4 -> heap, lock heap+0x58, call 0x0050E5B8(heap, block), unlock. Because the callee's own name is unreliable, the 'heap free' reading rests on the monitor offset and the handle dereference only, so keep maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ListRow_GetTextPixelWidth
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_ListRow_GetTextPixelWidth(void* self, int row, u32 third)
summary: Resolves a row's u16 text id from the row model at self+0x34 or from the data-manager table (0x0063DD38), then returns a size value: 0 when the id/row is absent, otherwise min(measure via 0x0011CFAC, 9) when 0x0062FC04 returns non-zero, else 9. The 0..9 clamp suggests a line/page class rather than raw pixels.
evidence: The twin 0x0062FC04 returns the other layout value and both are called by the poker windows (bl sites 0x001E560C and 0x001E617C checked in asm) before the two results are passed together to 0x003EA10C. What unit the clamped value has is still unproven, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Data_FindRowByPackedKeys
signature: u32 maybe_Data_FindRowByPackedKeys(void* self, u32 packedTableId, u32 packedKey, u32 arg4)
summary: Looks up a 0x28-byte row by three packed keys: the low byte of packedTableId selects the sub-table (0x0063F348), and rows match +0x20 u16 == packedTableId>>16, +0x22 u16 == packedKey&0xFFFF and +0x24 u8 == packedKey>>16. For table ids < 0x36 it falls back to the per-id record array at self+0x41C and only accepts rows whose +0x20 seen bit is set in work+0x2A444 and whose +0x22 byte matches work+0x27508. Returns the row or 0.
evidence: The key comparison and the seen-bit fallback are explicit in the body. The earlier 'story table' wording came from caller names that the call-graph index attributes through overlapping function spans (the 1708-byte extent of 0x0063D434 also contains 0x0063D790/0x0063D85C, and a checked caller e.g. 0x001C38C4 does not actually branch here), so the table identity is not proven.

name: Ui_GuideWindow_GetPageMessageId
summary: Returns the message id of the first entry in the guide window's page list (self+0x20) whose entry count byte exceeds the progress counter at work+0x27C88, or 0xFFFF when none does. Callers pass the result straight to Ui_GuideWindow_SetTextFromMessage as the page's message id.
evidence: All four bl sites are inside Ui_GuideWindow_Update/LayoutPage/SelectPageAction (0x003693F0, 0x00369430, 0x0036A228, 0x0036A520, checked in asm), and the call site at 0x003693F0 moves the return value into r1 for Ui_GuideWindow_SetTextFromMessage. The old 'Item_GetCountThresholdTag' name had both the subsystem and the return value wrong.

name: maybe_Ui_Part_GetRemainingAnimTime
summary: Returns the remaining animation time of a party member part: takes the total duration (0x00629280) and subtracts the per-entry durations (u8 at record+6) of up to 60 u16 record ids at self+0xA0 resolved through 0x0063CF74, stopping at 0xFFFF.
evidence: The body is total-minus-played arithmetic over the fixed 60-entry list, and both callers are skill-panel code; the direction (remaining vs already-spent) cannot be proven from the code alone, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ShouldShowByActorState
summary: Updates a battle actor window's visibility/state from its current action: clears bit 0x2000 of the actor's +0x270 word when the action model says so, asks Battle_ActorAction_UpdateReaction, and combines the result with the work flag at +0x27C57 and the window's f_6C0 byte to produce the show flag (returned through a dropped return value).
evidence: The body is readable through the named battle action helpers, but no caller or string pins which window it belongs to; the 'ShouldShowByActorState' reading is still a hypothesis about the returned flag, so keep maybe_ at low confidence.

name: Save_LoadWorkData
summary: Applies a stored save record to the live game: validates and compacts the item storage, applies the record with Save_ApplyRecordToWork, replays the pending EXP delta through Party_Member_AddExp, resets the member HP/state, re-applies the five saved equipment ids (<100) with 0x0035EBB0 and then rebuilds the trailing u16 id list.
evidence: Save_ApplyRecordToWork (0x0064CB24) is named and the body is the apply half (nothing writes a record out); the item/equipment re-application and the EXP delta are explicit. Which save container feeds the record is not proven, but the load-work-data role is.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ApplyWorkLayout
summary: Builds a 0x40-byte work block (16 zeroed words, then a 17-wchar string copied from data-table row 0xF0 through 0x00640200 and std_wcsncpy) and installs it into the save work at work+0x24A98 with 0x00613F14. Called from a map-window refresh helper; the body does not rebuild a layout.
evidence: The body only zeroes a local block, copies the 0x11-wchar string from row 0xF0 and calls the +0x24A98 installer; the caller 0x00624028 is itself unnamed, so the 'ApplyWorkLayout' wording overstates it and the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ListRow_HasTableLabel
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_ListRow_HasTableLabel(void* self, u16 rowId, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns 1 when the row's table model has an entry whose u16 id equals rowId, whose +8 relative string pointer is non-null, and for which the work-level lookup 0x0066B9BC(work+0x24A98,rowId) returns 0 (no work-supplied text). Returns 0 otherwise.
evidence: The body requires the table string to exist AND 0x0066B9BC to return 0 before returning 1, so the old 'HasTextOverride' name described the opposite condition. What 0x0066B9BC stores is inferred from its call site, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ListRow_DrawEquipComparisonA
signature: void maybe_Ui_ListRow_DrawEquipComparisonA(void* row, u32 memberIndex, u16* itemEntry, u32 stack)
summary: Equipment-comparison row renderer A: resolves the item through the 2H equip-category check 0x0066C5CC, builds the member stat context (Party_StatCalc_SetupMemberContext with 0x007C6F04) and formats the row with 0x0045A5A0(...,0) before tail-dispatching through the row-kind table at 0x00784318 indexed by row+4. No kind filter, unselected flag.
evidence: FACTS records 0x0066C5A8/0x0066C5CC as the 1H/2H equip-category checks, and the body then builds Party_StatCalc context and calls Item_RollStatBoostDelta, i.e. the stat-difference preview shown in the equip list. A/B/C differ only in category check, kind filter and selected flag, so the old 'DrawDispatch' wording said nothing.

name: maybe_Ui_ListRow_DrawEquipComparisonB
signature: void maybe_Ui_ListRow_DrawEquipComparisonB(void* row, u32 memberIndex, u16* itemEntry, u32 stack)
summary: Equipment-comparison row renderer B: resolves the item through the 1H equip-category check 0x0066C5A8, skips the row when the item record kind (+0x29) does not match the row's filter byte (+5), then builds the member stat context, formats with 0x0045A5A0(...,0) and tail-dispatches through 0x00784318. Unselected flag.
evidence: Same evidence as variant A (0x0066C5A8 is the 1H category check, Party_StatCalc + Item_RollStatBoostDelta build the comparison), with the additional +0x29-vs-row+5 filter visible in the body. The row-kind handler table is still unknown, so keep maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ListRow_DrawEquipComparisonC
signature: void maybe_Ui_ListRow_DrawEquipComparisonC(void* row, u32 memberIndex, u16* itemEntry, u32 stack)
summary: Equipment-comparison row renderer C (selected variant): requires the item record kind (+0x29) to equal the row filter byte (+5), resolves through the 1H check 0x0066C5A8, builds the member stat context, formats with 0x0045A5A0(...,1) and tail-dispatches through the table at 0x0078430C.

name: maybe_Ui_AbilityList_BuildEntryIds
